meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so you have about twenty minutes. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and when?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a weekend at home with the play open beside him, Hale, of course they read differently. I'm writing down September 24. Put both pieces in front of me.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Then it should never have been on the table to begin with. What does the version history show, with times? And did you look at any of it before the zero went in, or after?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero on Owen's essay withdrawn, an apology, and copies of his September 24 in-class writing and the version history you said you are relying on. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position with nothing agreed; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and to see the September 24 writing and the version history herself. The fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached; the meeting ended early, not on her clock.
What moved her: Comparing the essay with a dated piece of Owen's own in-class writing got her to write the date down, a first small sign of ground, because it was specific, dated and tied to his work, but it never moved her because she was never shown it.
What cost ground: Never answering who decided on the zero or why it went in before anyone called home, which is the procedural grievance she walked in with.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; Hale's evidence never got near that night, since the version history was mentioned but no times from it were given; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she opened by asking who decided on the zero, own in one sentence that it went in before you called her, then put the September 24 piece and the essay side by side in front of her so she can check them herself.
